newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says early data point to stronger Q2 GNP.
newsitem.headline: Manila says early data point to stronger Q2 GNP.

text.p: The Philippines is expected to turn out a stronger gross national product (GNP) growth in the second quarter compared with the 6.1 percent posted in the first quarter, Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said on Tuesday.
"All data are indicating that we can do better than first quarter," Habito told Reuters.
He said early economic figures such as the value of production index, the volume of production index and export performance indicated a robust growth.
"The growth rates are very encouraging, and we are just looking at the first month of the second quarter," he added.

The value of production index rose 9.3 percent, while the volume of production index increased 10.8 percent on an annual basis. The production indices are used as barometers on the output of the manufacturing sector.
The export sector grew year-on-year by 39 percent in April and 23 percent in May.
Habito also said output from the agriculture and services sectors remained strong.
The Philippines is expecting a seven to eight percent GNP growth in 1997 from 6.94 percent in 1996.
The official figures are scheduled to be released by the end of next month.
